optionReasons.saa-med-044:option:0: Change for SNS changes the model to unrowed pub/sub — does not resolve duplicity and still loses the processing buffer.
optionReasons.saa-med-044:option:1: Deleted before processing means losing the video if the consumer fails in the middle — the evaporate queue delivery guarantee.
optionReasons.saa-med-044:option:2: It's the closest because it moves exactly in the right parameter — only in the wrong direction: decreasing visibility timeout would make messages reappear yet MAIS early, multiplying the duplicates; the value needs to exceed the maximum processing time.

finalJustifications: Because the visibility timeout is greater than the processing (ex.: 12 min) keeps the message invisible while the video is processed — no other consumer receives it in parallel.
Because the biggest visibility timeout instructs the queue to delete the message by itself at the end of the deadline, exempting consumer confirmation.
Because the biggest visibility timeout reserves the original consumer for the message, and the queue redirects the others to new videos.
Because the highest visibility timeout activates the deduplication of the Standard row, which discards copies generated during processing.

optionReasons.saa-med-050:option:0: There's no such thing as 'Auto Scaling Volumes EBS' for snapshots — the Auto Scaling manages for instance fleets, not backups.
optionReasons.saa-med-050:option:1: CloudWatch Logs retain LOGS Applications — does not create or exhale volume snapshots.
optionReasons.saa-med-050:option:2: It is the closest because the concept is identical — life-cycle policies with transition and expiration — but the service is another: S3 Lifecycle acts on OBJETOS in pocket; snapshots EBS scheduled by tags and expired by retention are the Data Lifecycle Manager.

finalJustifications: Because DLM apply life cycle policies to snapshots and tags AMIs: create in the set schedule and expire those that pass from retention — complete automation.
Because DLM compresses old snapshots instead of excluding them, keeping the full coverage at a decreasing cost per month.
Because DLM converts expired snapshots into objects of the S3 Glacier, preserving the history outside the quota of EBS Account.
Because DLM requires the administrator's approval before each expiration, ensuring that no useful backup is lost.

optionReasons.saa-med-053:option:0: More memory reduces some errors, but does not eliminate flaws — and events that fail will continue to be discarded without trace.
optionReasons.saa-med-053:option:2: It's the closest because it's also a real configuration of asynchronous invocations — but zeroing attempts only makes events fail MAIS fast, still discarded; the requirement is to preserve them, paper from the failure destination (e.g.: row) SQS) with the context of the error.
optionReasons.saa-med-053:option:3: Print in the log does not preserve the event recessably — turn loose text into CloudWatch, without a row or structured context.

finalJustifications: Because on-failure destination sends the full event — with payload and error context — to a row SQS after exhausting the attempts: nothing is lost and the reprocessing becomes trivial.
Because the on-failure destination repeats the invocation of the function in a secondary region, where the code bug does not usually reproduce.
Because the destination on-failure reverses the original upload no S3 when the function fails, keeping the pocket and processing synchronized.
Because on-failure destination promotes the event for synchronous invocation, in which failures return directly to the original caller of S3.

optionReasons.saa-med-054:option:0: Internet Gateway in private sub-network the public make — changes the security design instead of solving the dependence.
optionReasons.saa-med-054:option:1: It's the closest because it adds redundancy of NAT for real — but in the wrong dimension: two NATs in MESMA AZ-1 fall together with the zone; dependence only dies with one NAT by AZ and each subnet routing to the one of the zone itself.
optionReasons.saa-med-054:option:2: Focus everything on AZ-1 transforms the VPC a single point of failure — the antithesis of multi-AZ resilience.

finalJustifications: Because one NAT Gateway by AZ, with each subnet roaming to the NAT local, eliminates cross-dependence: the fall of an area affects only its sub-networks.
Because the three of us NAT Gateways form an active-active cluster with shared IP, and traffic migrates alone in the fall of any area.
Because NAT by AZ triples the available output band of the VPC, and it is the capacity clearance that keeps the areas healthy in the air.
Because NAT by AZ synchronizes the active connections between the zones, allowing the failure of sessions without noticeable fall.

optionReasons.saa-med-056:option:0: The Trusted Advisor recommends cost and safety optimizations — does not inject any failure.
optionReasons.saa-med-056:option:2: It is the closest because Synthetics also 'tests' the application continuously — but with canaries that SIMULAM users to detect unavailability; it does not INJETA actual failures such as loss of instance or latency: controlled chaos experiments are the Fault Injection Service.
optionReasons.saa-med-056:option:3: Unannounced production is uncontrolled chaos: no stop conditions, no experiment — just a self-inflicted incident.

finalJustifications: Because FIS injects controlled real failures — finish instances, add latency, unavailability AZ — in experiments with automatic safety stop conditions.
Because FIS simulates faults in a mirrored environment of production, validating the reaction without touching the real resources of the application.
Because FIS monitors the chaos experiments performed by the team and recommends resilience corrections based on the results obtained.
Because FIS calendar random chaos windows without warning the team, measuring the genuine reaction of the operation to truly real incidents.

optionReasons.saa-med-057:option:1: Retention period defines how long the message stays in the queue — does not prevent duplicate deliveries.
optionReasons.saa-med-057:option:2: Processing twice as purposely multiplies exactly the effect you want to avoid — repeated collections have become rule.
optionReasons.saa-med-057:option:3: It is the closest because a single consumer actually reduces the duplication windows — but does not eliminate them (the Standard row can duplicate the ENTREGA even with a consumer) and destroys scalability; the correct design is identical by unique identifier.

finalJustifications: Because Idempotence attacks the effect: before charging, the consumer checks by the unique identifier if the request has already been processed — the duplicate arrives, but does not charge twice.
Because Idempotence instructs the queue itself to compare the hash of each message and discard copies before delivery to the consumer.
Because the same request is grouped together in a single consolidated delivery, processed at once by the designated consumer.
Because the Idempotence automatically stifles the second charge when detecting the repeated identifier at the end of batch processing.

optionReasons.saa-med-061:option:0: It's the closest because Scheduler also shoots events in EventBridge — But it creates events NOVOS in cron calendars; does not store or forward past bus events, which is the role of the archive with replay.
optionReasons.saa-med-061:option:2: Depending on manual resend of origins does not scale and is not always possible — many systems do not keep what they have issued.
optionReasons.saa-med-061:option:3: More rules route future events to more destinations — do not bring back any past events.

finalJustifications: Because the archive records the events that pass through the bus and the replay sends them on demand to the chosen period — the reprocessing becomes a console operation.
Because the archive exports events to S3 in real time, and the replay reimports them by API Intake lot of the bus.
Because the archive keeps consumers in the mirror during retention, reapplying events when detecting state divergence.
Because the replay re-executes the rules of the bus over the logs of CloudTrail, reconstructing the original events of the requests.

optionReasons.saa-med-069:option:1: It's the closest because it points in the right direction — the gp3 actually released the IOPS size — but exaggerated: there are limits (up to 16.000 IOPS by volume gp3); what has changed is that now IOPS and throughput are PROVISIONAL regardless of size, not infinite.
optionReasons.saa-med-069:option:2: The gp3 is available for instances EC2 in general — no bar metal restriction.
optionReasons.saa-med-069:option:3: Forum Store is another type of storage (eminent and local) — it is not prerequisite for anything in EBS.

finalJustifications: Because in gp3 as IOPS and throughput are provideable dimensions apart: the 10.000 IOPS can be configured in the same 500 GB, without inflating the volume as in gp2.
Because the gp3 inherits the accumulated burst credits from the gp2, and it is they who sustain the 10.000 IOPS without increasing the size.
Because gp3 uses the RAM host as a writing cache, delivering IOPS in addition to the physical disk for volumes of any size.
Because gp3 partitions the volume into internal shards of 100 GB, and each shard adds its share of IOPS Total available.
